findings.bug: setCredentialsProviderClassName assigns the given class name to the wrong field: it writes this.exceptionOverrideClassName instead of this.credentialsProviderClassName (copy-paste from setExceptionOverrideClassName).
findings.why_real: The field credentialsProviderClassName (declared line 77) is read by getCredentialsProviderClassName() (line 878) but is never assigned anywhere; line 893 instead clobbers exceptionOverrideClassName. Compare the sibling setExceptionOverrideClassName (line 946) which correctly assigns exceptionOverrideClassName, and setDriverClassName which assigns its own field. So after calling this setter the getter for the intended property returns null AND an unrelated property is corrupted.
findings.how_to_prove: HikariConfig c = new HikariConfig(); c.setCredentialsProviderClassName("com.zaxxer.hikari.pool.TestCredentialsProvider"); assertEquals("com.zaxxer.hikari.pool.TestCredentialsProvider", c.getCredentialsProviderClassName()); // expected: that class name, actual: null. Also assertNull(c.getExceptionOverrideClassName()); // expected: null, actual: the credentials-provider class name (corrupted).

findings.bug: Deprecation-warning version guard uses '>= 1' on String.compareTo, so the warning is NOT emitted for the exact version 4.3.6 even though the message and intent say 'Hibernate 4.3.6 and newer'.
findings.why_real: For version string "4.3.6", substring(0,5).compareTo("4.3.6") returns 0, and 0 >= 1 is false, so the branch is skipped. compareTo returns a sign (negative/zero/positive), not increments of 1, so the only correct threshold for 'this version or newer' is '>= 0'. The immediately-following log message explicitly claims coverage of '4.3.6 and newer', contradicting the guard.
findings.how_to_prove: If Version.getVersionString() returns "4.3.6", constructing HikariConnectionProvider should log the deprecation warning; with '>= 1' it does not. Expected: warning logged for 4.3.6; actual: not logged (only logged for versions lexicographically greater, e.g. 4.3.7).
